correctness.rationale: For all integers k>=3 the product U_1...U_k has kth moment (n+1)^(-k), making its order-two generalized Cauchy transform z^(-1)Li_{k-1}(1/z). The published Markov–Krein identity gives exact H_k=-G_k’/(2G_k), producing the quotient. The strictly nonzero polylog denominator boundary imaginary part yields local Stieltjes inversion on (0,1); the endpoint residue gives a mass exactly 1/2 at zero, none at one, and no remaining singular mass. Explicit branch-cut asymptotics prove the left coefficient (k-1)/2 and the right exponent k-3 including k=3. The first two raw moments follow by Laurent coefficients. The embedded checker executed 45 deterministic numerical tests; no universal conclusion relies on finite tests.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is for ALL INTEGER POWERS k>=3. Mergny 2026 Theorem 1.4(ii) gives existence, injectivity and a general logarithmic derivative, not the explicit polylogarithmic density and sharp boundary classification. Mergny 2022 Eq. (12) implies the k=2 logistic-Cauchy special case after squaring and 1/2 mixing: that special case is EXCLUDED FROM NEW CLAIM. James 2010 beta-scaling gives a related identity, but not the k>=3 transform evaluations and endpoint limits. Relevant published-finding corpus queries and searches in published mathematical records showed no directly covering k>=3 result; absence of hits alone is not an originality proof. value.rationale: The class is motivated by the natural iterated multiplicative convolution of the most elementary nontrivial base law at the first integer Markov–Krein order. Existence alone does not specify the inverse distribution. For the whole infinite hierarchy k>=3 the result identifies a nonvanishing half atom as mean tends to zero, exact positive density via polylogarithms, and distinct right-edge orders (positive finite at k=3 and vanishing at increasing orders for k>=4), with a universal logarithmic left singularity. This is a complete natural family classification with explicitly motivated endpoint invariants and a route to exact sampling/numerical evaluation, not an arbitrary slice. The earlier known k=2 case is not used as novelty evidence.
